articles.title: Coventry 3-2 Crystal Palace: Dwight McNeil own goal hands Sky Blues important win and Thomas Frank a losing start with Eagles
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Palace fall to a fifth straight Premier League loss; new boss Thomas Frank saw his side twice come from behind but Dwight McNeil's unfortunate own goal proves costly; Coventry make it back-to-back home wins to go 13th; Palace stay bottom
articles.body:
Palace twice came from behind to level the match - but Coventry wouldn't be denied. A long throw launched into the Palace box with five minutes to play was flicked on and Dean Henderson could only bounce Brandon Thomas-Asante's shot against McNeil and into the goal.

It was a messy way to decide a game which had been lit up in the first half by some exceptional goals but Sky Blues boss Frank Lampard and his side's supporters won't care about that. They've won back-to-back home games and are now three points clear of the Premier League drop zone in 13th.

In contrast, Frank's return to the dugout with Palace was ultimately a painful one, despite some encouraging signs. There was excellent link-up play between Jorgen Strand Larsen and Yeremy Pino for the two Palace goals but they have now lost five Premier League games on the spin and stay rock bottom of the table.

The 27 goals Palace have conceded in the league this season is their worst record after 11 games since 1927/28 and a major issue for Frank to address, following his arrival as Pierre Sage's replacement earlier this week.

This is a game which could have gone either way after a thrilling first 45 minutes. Coventry scored two super goals, with Taiwo Awoniyi slotting in after some fine play from Yann Gboho and Jack Rudoni before the latter found Tatsuhiro Sakamoto on the edge of the box to fire into the top corner.

At the other end, Strand Larsen's scorpion-kick assist for Palace's first goal was stunning; Pino returned the favour on the stroke of half-time with a beautiful lobbed pass of his own.

The second half couldn't live up to the first and the final goal was the scrappiest of the lot. But it will be one treasured by Lampard and Coventry, who have nine points from a possible 12 in their past four home games. They are heading in the right direction. The challenge for Frank is to tighten his defence up and find similar momentum at Palace.

"We had to fight for it today. It was a difficult match. New manager bounce, a good feeling about them, they played pretty well. It was a tight game in many aspects.

"The spirit of our boys, the impact of the subs was big for us. It's good for us to feel that. We need that spirit to get to where we need to. Delighted to win it.

"We've been out of the league 25 years. The steps we've taken so quickly, for the boys to get accustomed to it, it's good for the feeling. We can't get too excited. But it's nice since our first four games, we didn't get anything, since then we've got good points and performances."

"This was definitely clear this was the Premier League. The tempo, intensity, the mad moments and so on.

"It wasn't the result we hoped for. I think what I'd praise the players for was the intensity, the willingness, the running power, the effort in every aspect.

"Satisfied we scored two good goals and created good chances.

"The first half we were a bit too open. The second half much more in control. We limited Coventry to basically their goal - which we should have avoided as well.

"I felt in the second half it was us closer to scoring the goal than Coventry."

articles.title: Man City 1-1 Fulham: Elliot Anderson equaliser ends losing streak but City held amid Erling Haaland goal debate
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Elliot Anderson cancelled out Rodrigo Muniz's early goal but Man City could only draw 1-1 with Fulham at the Etihad Stadium; Erling Haaland had a first-half goal ruled out for a foul on Bernd Leno that divided opinion
articles.body:
Elliot Anderson volleyed City level early in the second half after Erling Haaland had seen a first-half equaliser controversially ruled out. But Alvaro Arbeloa's Fulham were well worth a point, Rodrigo Muniz's fine opener setting the tone for an enterprising display.

There was frustration among the City players and supporters when Haaland looked to have bundled in the equaliser soon after Muniz's goal but referee Thomas Bramall ruled that the Norwegian striker had fouled Bernd Leno and the VAR did not overrule him.

The ambition of Fulham's approach merited some fortune. They were aggressive out of possession and confident enough to play when they had the ball - which was plenty. Former City man Oscar Bobb should have doubled the advantage before the interval.

Enzo Maresca had responded to the defeat away to Nottingham Forest, in which City's vulnerability on transition was a striking feature of the game, by bringing in Ayyoub Bouaddi for Enzo Fernandez. But Fulham had little problem playing through them.

The response eventually came through Anderson. It was not just his spectacular volley through a crowd of bodies. He was racing through on goal as City chased a winner, going close with a left-footed effort that drifted just wide of the post, driving his team on.

City still needed Gianluigi Donnarumma at the other end, saving from Muniz and Calvin Bassey, whose presence in the box following a breakaway summed up Fulham's intent. They did more than hold on, and David Affengruber continually bested a below-par Haaland.

The draw extends improving Fulham's unbeaten run to five matches and does at least end City's three-game losing streak under Maresca. But the Italian coach continues to have problems to solve on this evidence. They remain third, below Brighton in second.

Man City head coach Enzo Maresca speaking in the press conference:

"I reviewed the goal after the game and from my point of view it is quite clear that it is not a foul but I am not the guy who decides, unfortunately.

"[Erling] was absolutely sure even when they were reviewing the VAR that it is a goal because I asked from the touchline but the referee decides differently."

Asked about playing Ayyoub Bouaddi in a deeper role with Elliot Anderson :

"Ayyoub with Elliot were both really good. Today, we used Elliot a bit more as an attacking midfielder, he arrived inside the box and scored a fantastic goal, and he had three or four moments around the box where he was really dangerous.

"It is another solution for us. In this moment, we are trying to know each other more and also to find the right solution.

"We use him today for the first time since the season start as an attacking midfielder. He was playing a little bit more deep with us. We are trying to find different solutions, right balance, and to be more consistent."

Fulham head coach Alvaro Arbeloa speaking in the press conference:

"I told them we would have the chance to beat them if we played with courage, with character. I won the last time I was here [with Real Madrid] so I thought maybe we would have the chance to beat Man City.

"We knew also they lost the last three games. I think we perform really well. We could win the game.

"Obviously, they are amazing players, an amazing team but I told my players that if we want to beat them we need to be our best, be aggressive, don't give them the ball so easily."

Asked about the decision to disallow Haaland's goal:

"Leno told me that, Haaland, it was a foul so I prefer not to talk about the referee and the yellow cards because last time I spoke about the referee it wasn't good for me, I need to save money so I prefer to talk about my players."

Nobody gets the better of Fulham 18 times in a row. Their long sequence of 17 defeats to Manchester City finally came to an end and they deserved their draw. Arbeloa's commitment to a possession game is impressive and starting to get its rewards.

The Spaniard was under pressure after an unconvincing start that contrasted with Maresca's seven-game winning streak to start the campaign. But while their teams could not be separated, it is Arbeloa's Fulham's looking more confident and purposeful.

They had to play through press, not easy to do even if City did look a little disjointed. And they defended both resolutely - and bravely. Bassey was prepared to follow Phil Foden deep into opposition territory. Affengruber was trusted to face Haaland one-against-one.

It was bold and had Fulham been punished it would have been easy to say - and indeed write - that it was expecting too much of his team. But the Fulham players' belief in this style of play is growing. They are five unbeaten after that shaky start. Promising form.

articles.title: 'I'll be back fresh and ready': Harry Kane vows stronger comeback after serious ankle injury
articles.summary: Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane is determined to turn his latest injury setback into an opportunity to come back stronger, insisting he will return
articles.body: Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane is determined to turn his latest injury setback into an opportunity to come back stronger, insisting he will return refreshed and ready for the crucial phase of the season in 2027. The England captain suffered a serious ankle injury during Bayern's 1-1 Bundesliga draw against Cologne on Friday, with the club confirming that he will be sidelined for several months.Kane took to social media to address the setback, expressing his disappointment while underlining his determination to overcome the challenge. The 33-year-old sustained a tear to the syndesmotic ligament in his left ankle, ruling him out of action for an extended period."The highs and lows of life! Obviously very disappointed to get this injury, but as always it's an opportunity to show resilience and improvement going into 2027. I'll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season!" Kane wrote.Kane draws inspiration from former NFL starThe Bayern forward also shared an encouraging message he received from former NFL player Julian Edelman, using it as motivation to deal with the difficult phase of his career."'Tough times don't last, tough people do' – my guy @Edelman11 told me this one!" Kane added.The England captain also thanked supporters for their messages and wishes following the injury, ending his post with the German phrase "Alles gut", which translates to "All good".How did Harry Kane suffer the ankle injury?Kane picked up the injury shortly after Bayern fell behind against Cologne when defender Joel Schmied's challenge caught his left ankle. The striker attempted to continue playing but was eventually forced off in the 20th minute, with Tom Bischof replacing him.Bayern later confirmed the extent of the injury, announcing that Kane had suffered a tear to the syndesmotic ligament in his left ankle. The German champions also suffered another injury concern during the contest, with French winger Michael Olise sustaining a bruised forefoot. No stranger to pulling off wacky antics on College Gameday , Pat McAfee wasted no time getting things started during Saturday's broadcast from Miami.

articles.title: Arbeloa agrava la crisis galopante del Manchester City
articles.standfirst: Cuarto partido consecutivo de Premier sin ganar para los 'sky blues'
articles.summary: Cuarto partido consecutivo de Premier sin ganar para los 'sky blues'
articles.body: Mientras uno sale de la crisis, otro entra de lleno en ella. El Fulham de Arbeloa ya acumula cinco partidos consecutivos sin conocer la derrota en Premier League y se aleja del descenso. Y aunque son tres empates seguidos (todos 1-1), desde Craven Cottage el 'proyecto Arbeloa' ya se mira con otros ojos. En Mánchester, mientras, a la espera de la posible sanción histórica por incumplir las reglas financieras de la Premier, entran en barrena. El City de Maresca, después de encadenar siete triunfos consecutivos en un arranque de Premier League histórico, ha encallado. Desde aquel 3-2 al Ipswich a mediados de octubre, los 'sky blues' no ganan en la liga inglesa: derrota ante el Villa, derrota ante el Brighton, derrota en Nottingham con el Forest y, ahora, tras el parón, empate en casa ante el Fulham. Un bajón que da aires a un Arsenal que, en caso de ganar, se escaparía con ocho puntos sobre los 'cityzens'. El 'pinchazo' de hoy, mientras, se fraguó 'desde dentro'. Fue un ex como Oscar Bobb el que construyó la jugada del 0-1. Rodrigo Muniz, titular por delante de Gonzalo en el Etihad, anotó el primero con un disparo precioso a la escuadra. El City, que fue dominador el resto del encuentro, no tenía capacidad para generar ante un Fulham que se defendía bien. A Haaland, mientras, le anularon un gol por falta sobre Leno. Fue en la segunda parte, rozando la hora de partido, cuando Elliot Anderson, que venía de ser expulsado ante España en la Nations, anotó de volea desde la frontal. Aprovechó un despeje para, por fin, desbaratar la resistencia londinense. Un empate que coloca al Fulham, por ahora, con tres puntos de ventaja sobre el descenso. El City, mientras, se aleja de la cabeza... y ve como Liverpool o Chelsea podrían echársele encima.

articles.title: El Sabadell frena en su fortín la racha triunfal del Granada, pero sigue sin ganar
articles.standfirst: Los arlequinados, a los que anularon dos goles, se mantienen invictos en casa, mientras los nazaríes no pueden sumar su séptima victoria seguida
articles.summary: Los arlequinados, a los que anularon dos goles, se mantienen invictos en casa, mientras los nazaríes no pueden sumar su séptima victoria seguida
articles.body: El Granada de Pacheta puso fin a su racha triunfal de seis victorias ligueras consecutivas con un empate en el fortín de la Nova Creu Alta. Un gol de Alain Ribeiro en la recta final le permite al Sabadell recuperar un punto y, sobre todo, evitar su primer derrota como local al nivelar el tanto de Alemañ. Los arlequinados, que vieron cómo les anulaban sendos goles de Édgar y Yanis Rahmani, enlazan seis jornadas sin ganar y cuatro empates seguidos en casa, pese a firmar un gran encuentro sobreponiéndose a la plaga de bajas y dando un nuevo pasito hacia el objetivo de la permanencia. El Sabadell quería dar continuidad a la goleada balsámica en la Copa del Rey y saltó al césped con una marcha más. Volvió a ser el equipo de las primeras jornadas y pudo adelantarse en los primeros minutos por mediación de Yanis Rahmani y sobre todo de Edgar González, que se quedó solo ante el gol tras un error del meta Alberto Flores que por evitar un córner le dejó el balón franco, pero el central no atinó a marcar a puerta vacía ante la llegada del otro Flores, Juanjo, que taponó su remate. Los arlequinados, liderados por Ángel Baena, mostraban su cara más vertical e incisiva y eran superiores, ante un rival frustrado e incómodo pese a las ocasiones iniciales de Rodelas y Gumbau. La primera acción decisiva llegó a la media hora. Edgar marcó desde la frontal, con un disparo que desvió Lama, pero los jugadores del Granada rodearon a Rafael Sánchez para reclamar un agarrón y una mano de Óscar Sanz sobre Kader Bamba en la jugada anterior. El defensa arlequinado era último hombre y el extremo francés corría solo hacia Diego Fuoli. Se podía pasar del gol local a la expulsión local. Después de cinco minutos de revisión el colegiado optó por el camino del medio, sin contentar a nadie: ni gol ni expulsión. Y poco después llegó el 0-1 cuando Alemañ remató a placer una asistencia de Jorge Pascual tras una gran acción por la izquierda. El Granada no había sido mejor, pero ganaba ante un rival que volvía a acosar su falta de pólvora. Los visitantes pudieron sentenciar en el inicio del segundo acto, pero Fuoli firmó una parada extraordinaria para repeler un remate franco de Rodelas, tras gran centro de Bamba. El Sabadell celebró el empate acto seguido, en una transición canónica, vertiginosa, por mediación de Yanis Rahmani, pero el árbitro volvió a anular el gol, por un claro fuera de juego de Baena en la asistencia. Siguió insistiendo el equipo arlequinado, pero Alberto Flores respondió con un paradón al cabezazo de Édgar tras un córner y otro testarazo de Alain Ribeiro se marchó alto. Pero los locales consiguieron finalmente su premio en la recta final cuando Alain Ribeiro convirtió un disparo desviado de Yanis Rahmani en una asistencia y celebró el 1-1, tan merecido. Los locales rozaron la remontada con un cabezazo desde cerca del propio Ribeiro, pero de nuevo lo evitó Alberto Flores con otro paradón.

articles.title: Premier League: 14 years, 20 defeats — Fulham finally end Man City's dominance with a draw
articles.summary: Manchester City's long-standing dominance over Fulham came to an end on Saturday as the two sides played out a 1-1 draw at the Etihad Stadium, extending
articles.body: Manchester City's long-standing dominance over Fulham came to an end on Saturday as the two sides played out a 1-1 draw at the Etihad Stadium, extending their winless run in the Premier League to four matches.The result ended Fulham's 20-match losing streak against City in all competitions, dating back to 2012, and brought an end to a remarkable 14-year run of defeats against the Manchester club.City avoided a fourth successive league defeat but once again delivered an unconvincing performance, dropping more points in the title race. They remain third in the standings, five points behind leaders Arsenal, who can extend their advantage with a win against Newcastle United later on Saturday.Muniz strikes before Anderson rescues a pointFulham made a bright start and took the lead in the 16th minute through Rodrigo Muniz, who finished clinically after being set up by former City player Oscar Bobb.City thought they had equalised eight minutes later when Erling Haaland bundled the ball over the line after Fulham goalkeeper Bernd Leno had saved his initial close-range effort. However, VAR ruled out the goal, judging that Haaland had kicked the ball out of Leno's hands.The Premier League later explained that Leno was deemed to be "in control of the ball".Haaland had earlier wasted two good opportunities, underlining City's struggles in front of goal as Fulham defended resolutely.The hosts eventually found their breakthrough in the 57th minute when Elliott Anderson produced a superb volley from the edge of the area. His effort flew through a crowd of players and into the bottom corner, earning City a point and marking his first Premier League goal since joining from Nottingham Forest.Both sides had opportunities to snatch a winner. Muniz was denied by City goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma, while Fulham continued to threaten on the counter-attack.The visitors, however, held on for a deserved point and a landmark result against their long-time tormentors.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 22-time Grand Slam champion Rafael Nadal elected to Real Madrid Board of Directors with 99.5 per cent votes
articles.summary: Tennis legend Rafael Nadal has added a new chapter to his illustrious sporting journey, this time away from the court, after being elected to the Real
articles.body: Tennis legend Rafael Nadal has added a new chapter to his illustrious sporting journey, this time away from the court, after being elected to the Real Madrid Board of Directors with an overwhelming majority of votes. The 22-time Grand Slam champion's appointment was ratified at the Spanish football club's Extraordinary General Assembly on Friday, with 99.5 per cent of the votes cast in his favour.A total of 1,713 votes were recorded, of which 1,704 supported Nadal's appointment, while four voted against and five abstained. The announcement was met with a standing ovation from the club's representatives, underlining the affection and respect the Spanish sporting icon commands among Real Madrid supporters.Nadal, who has been an honorary member of Real Madrid since 2011, described his new role as both an honour and a significant responsibility, expressing his desire to contribute to the continued success of one of the world's biggest sporting institutions.Florentino Perez hails Nadal's appointment as special moment for Real MadridReal Madrid president Florentino Perez welcomed Nadal's induction into the board, describing the occasion as a special moment for the club. He also praised the tennis great's achievements, character and longstanding association with the Spanish giants."We all know the extraordinary stature of Rafa Nadal. His name is already part of the universal history of sport. He has achieved something that is within reach of very few: becoming a legend admired and respected in every corner of the world," Perez said, as quoted in the club's official statement.The Real Madrid president also highlighted Nadal's connection with the club, pointing to his passion for the team and his association with its values."Rafa is a person who has earned the respect and affection of millions of people because of his character, his behaviour on and off the courts, and his unwavering commitment to the values that make sport great. And for us there is something that has a very special meaning: Rafa is one of our own. He is an honorary member of Real Madrid, he feels deeply about these colours and has always proudly expressed his Madridismo," he added.Perez further expressed confidence that Nadal's presence would help the club maintain its identity and continue building for future generations.Nadal calls new role an honour and responsibilityResponding to his appointment, Nadal said joining the Real Madrid Board of Directors was a moment of immense pride, while acknowledging the responsibility that came with representing a globally recognised sporting institution."It's a great responsibility to be part of the Real Madrid Board of Directors. This club is passed down from parents to children and unites people. For me, it unites me with my family and friends to watch the matches together. It's a great honour and a great source of satisfaction," Nadal said.The former world No. 1 also underlined his intention to contribute to the club's continued success, while expressing his understanding of the expectations attached to his new position."I am very aware of the responsibility because Real Madrid is a global brand. It is an immense responsibility, and I accept it so that over time I can learn and contribute to ensuring that this club remains the best in the world," he added.Nadal also reiterated his commitment to helping Real Madrid preserve its status as one of the most successful clubs in world football."I'm going to work to ensure things stay the way they are: a successful club, and that it continues to be so in the years to come. Hala Madrid," he said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Malachi Toney 'Created in a Lab, Outer Space, X-Men Type Stuff,' Says Miami's Cristobal in New Video
articles.summary: As Malachi Toney continues to work his way back from a high-ankle sprain that required surgery, Miami head coach Mario Cristobal praised his star wide receiver's recovery skills.
articles.body:
As Malachi Toney continues to work his way back from a high-ankle sprain that required surgery, Miami head coach Mario Cristobal praised his star wide receiver's recovery skills.

Appearing on ESPN's College Gameday , Cristobal described Toney as being "created in a lab, outer space, X-Men type stuff."

Toney also appeared on the ESPN broadcast with Jess Sims to offer an update on his rehab, noting he is getting closer to running at full speed.

Toney injured his ankle during a Hurricanes practice earlier this month and the recovery time from surgery is usually around four weeks.

Cristobal said Friday on The Pat McAfee Show he felt like Toney was "really close" and "probably about a week and a half out" from returning.

This could have Toney back in time for the ACC Championship Game on Dec. 5. Miami can clinch a spot in the conference title game on Saturday with a win over Virginia Tech or a Louisville loss.

Toney was on the Heisman shortlist prior to his injury with 73 receptions, 1,027 yards and 13 touchdowns in eight games.

articles.title: Tottenham 2-0 Ipswich: Teenager Luca Williams-Barnett scores on first Spurs start as 18-year-old shines
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as teenager Luca Williams-Barnett stars in Tottenham's 2-0 home win over Ipswich; the 18-year-old made Spurs history with his 15th-minute opener; England U19 international then involved in Dominic Solanke's second-half goal as Ipswich go five without a win
articles.body:
The 18-year-old bundled home the opener at the back post in the 15th minute to become the youngest Spurs player to score on his first Premier League start for the club.

The Spurs academy graduate then turned provider in the second half as he terrorised the Ipswich defence from his left-wing position to tee up Dominic Solanke with a low cross for a simple 51st-minute finish.

But Ipswich goalkeeper Christian Walton's diversion into Solanke's path meant Williams-Barnett was not credited with the assist officially.

It meant Williams-Barnett, at the age of 18 years 51 days, just missed out on becoming the second-youngest player to both score and assist in a Premier League game (Michael Owen in December 1997 at 17y 364d).

The teenager was substituted in the 64th minute to a standing ovation and rapturous cheers from the Spurs fans, who had serenaded Williams-Barnett with Harry Kane's 'He's one of our own' chant - raising hopes that the club may have unearthed a new academy hero.

The England U19 international's dazzling display inspired Tottenham to a third consecutive home league victory for the first time in two years, lifting Roberto De Zerbi's side to ninth and within three points of the top five.

But the Italian had to watch the deserved win from the stands as he served a one-game touchline ban after receiving three yellow cards this season.

His opposite number Gary O'Neil, meanwhile, saw his side's winless run extend to five games as Ipswich rarely threatened the home side to leave the Tractor Boys in 16th and just two points above the relegation zone.

De Zerbi: 'Special' Williams-Barnett a similar talent to Lamine Yamal

Spurs head coach De Zerbi believes Williams-Barnett is a "special player" and is a similar talent to Barcelona teenage sensation Lamine Yamal.

De Zerbi said at his post-match press conference: "He is a special player. I'm not surprised because his talent is bigger than you think.

"He played very well. He's lucky because he's playing in a top club with top team-mates.

"Yesterday evening, when I gave the first 11 to the players, I said, 'remember your debut and help the kid tomorrow, because he's one of us and if he plays well, we have more chances to win the game'.

"He's very young but at the same time he's a mature guy. He understands the right behaviour to keep in the dressing room - and he's older than his age."

He added: "The first day I spoke with Luca, I asked him two things: to play like he plays on the park with his friends, with the same freedom and to play and to work hard without the ball, like [Ousmane] Dembele, like Raphinha, like [Lamine] Yamal, because football is going in a different way and the first defenders are really the attackers even if they are Ballon d'Or or now the wingers or any players with talent, they have to work on the pitch."

Then asked whether Williams-Barnett is a special talent like PSG's Ballon d'Or winner Dembele and Spain's World Cup-winner Lamine Yamal, De Zerbi replied: "Yes, I think so.

"One of the best things in my career as a player, I've seen today on the bus from the training ground to the stadium. He was very close to me on the bus, and while we were coming to the stadium, he was watching Ronaldinho and Hazard on YouTube.

"I thought he was a special guy because, one hour and 30 minutes before your debut in the Premier League, you are watching Ronaldinho, [Eden] Hazard, Neymar, all this type of talent.

"Football is magic, no? The qualities, okay, but also the passion - you understand football, how football can be."

What a memorable full debut for Williams-Barnett.

After a handful of encouraging substitute displays this season, the 18-year-old was deservedly handed his first Spurs start - and boy did he take it.

He dazzled on the left wing to become the youngest Spurs player to score in the Premier League since Gareth Bale against Fulham in September 2007 (18y 47d).

Bale would go on to become a Spurs great, and there will be optimism that Williams-Barnett can do the same.

Every time he touched the ball in the win over Ipswich, there was real excitement at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, which has been in short supply in recent times.

He was a constant threat to the Ipswich defence as defenders backed off him, which exactly led to Solanke's goal.

The stats back up his impressive performance - he had the most touches in the opposition box (8) and big chances (2) of any player, while no player had more than his four shots on target.

For all of Spurs' big summer spending, their new hero looks to be from within.

articles.standfirst: Segunda derrota consecutiva de los 'blues'... y esta con goleada en contra en casa
articles.summary: Segunda derrota consecutiva de los 'blues'... y esta con goleada en contra en casa
articles.body: Ni empezar ganando 1-0 'salvó' al Chelsea. El tanto de Emegha, su primero con el Chelsea en su primera titularidad en Premier, fue insuficiente y los problemas defensivos volvieron a lastrar a un equipo, el 'blue', que se desmorona. Se fueron al parón con derrota ante el Sunderland... y ahora el Leeds, que venció 1-4 en Stamford Bridge levantando música de viento y protestas, agrava la crisis. 20 goles encajados en 11 jornadas confirman a la peor defensa del top-14 en Inglaterra. Una debacle. Fue una nueva película de terror el encuentro del Chelsea a nivel defensivo y ni el retorno del 'Dibu' Martínez sirvió para ordenar la zaga. Acheampong, Fofana, Colwill y Pep Chavarría fueron los elegidos de inicio por un Xabi Alonso que, evidentemente, tiene un problema serio. Y el Leeds lo aprovechó. Okafor firmó un doblete con dos remates de buen delantero centro. El ex Milan encontró los huecos en una defensa pasiva y descolocada, y fusiló al 'Dibu'. De penalti, antes de la sentencia de Okafor, anotó Calvert-Lewin tras una mano de Morgan Rogers. Cuando todo parecía ya cerrado y la herida no podía ser más profunda, Aaronson se inventó un golazo al contragolpe. Un 1-4 muy doloroso para Xabi. El Chelsea, que además perdió a Moisés Caicedo por lesión, se descuelga con esta nueva derrota: son octavos a dos puntos del Bournemouth, equipo que marca ahora mismo la 'zona Champions'... pero podría quedarse a cinco del top-4 si el Liverpool gana el domingo ante el Manchester United. El Leeds, mientras, ya es sexto.

articles.title: Chelsea 1-4 Leeds: Blues dismantled as pressure grows on manager Xabi Alonso after Noah Okafor's double
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Leeds beat Chelsea in the Premier League; Noah Okafor scored twice after Emmanuel Emegha had given hosts lead; Dominic Calvert-Lewin put Leeds ahead with a penalty; Brenden Aaronson capped Leeds' first victory at Stamford Bridge since 1999
articles.body:
Chelsea were booed off at half-time and full-time after suffering their third Premier League defeat in four games, a run which has seen them slip to eighth, as Leeds earned their first victory at Stamford Bridge since 1999.

Alonso's side have also been dumped out of the Carabao Cup and are already without European football this season.

Emmanuel Emegha gave the hosts a first-half lead on his first start, but Noah Okafor deservedly equalised before half-time, and Leeds ran riot after the break. Dominic Calvert-Lewin put the visitors ahead with a penalty, Okafor smashed in his second and Brenden Aaronson capped an outstanding away win to move Leeds sixth.

Four of Chelsea's five league defeats have now come without the injured Joao Pedro with his absence felt again despite Emegha smashing in the opener. The 23-year-old, making only his third appearance, caught James Trafford out at his near post although the striker was starved of service.

His goal came after Moises Caicedo was forced off following a heavy fall, and against the run of play after Calvert-Lewin had sent a header against the crossbar, but Leeds equalised within three minutes.

Calvert-Lewin slipped in Okafor, who with three Chelsea defenders around him in the box still managed to send a low, left-footed shot through the legs of Levi Colwill, across Emi Martínez and into the bottom right corner.

From there, Leeds were dominant until the end. Calvert-Lewin flicked a shot just wide, had a header saved, and Tarik Muharemovic's goal was ruled out for offside, all before half-time. Chelsea got worse still after the break.

Martinez's return in goal did little to settle a shaky defence, which was under pressure right from the restart, before Jayden Bogle's rocket struck the right arm of Morgan Rogers and referee Michael Oliver pointed to the spot. Calvert-Lewin sent Martinez the wrong way after VAR had backed the on-field decision following a lengthy check.

Chelsea never once looked like being able to recover and Leeds soon added a third. Ethan Ampadu's low cross from the right deflected up into the middle, and Okafor slammed a close-range volley into the top-left corner in the 58th minute.

It was too soon for the home fans to head for the exits, but they groaned every time Chelsea lost the ball, and a few boos followed Alonso's substitutions before they left en masse when Aaronson tucked in a fourth in added time.

Alonso: We're fragile and don't recover when punched

"After the equaliser, after the change [Caicedo], we lost the momentum completely. Until then, we were doing okay. We were creating, we were coming out from the pressure, but from that moment they started believing and we started not believing and it changed totally.

"And after that, we never got the good feeling mentality at any moment, and we were not able to cope with the pressure, and we didn't get close to the goal, so it completely changed it.

"We need to find solutions for sure because there will be setbacks during any game and to be tougher and to be able to go through that and to know that it's still so long to play, it's something mandatory in this competition.

"Today I felt that probably we are in a fragile moment mentally, confidence, when we receive a punch that we don't recover that strong, that tough enough."

Calvert-Lewin: Chelsea couldn't handle intensity

"I expected Chelsea to come out with a bit more oomph in the second half. But our intensity and the way that we played and the way that we set up against them, they couldn't handle it. That reflected in the scoreline."

Farke: We dominated - I can't wait to watch it back

"Great performance. I would have been disappointed with a draw today. I was a bit disappointed even at half-time when it was just a draw because from the first to the last [minute], we were the better side.

"We dominated this game, made sure that our plan for this game worked. We wanted to play on the front foot; we wanted to press Chelsea high; we wanted to make sure that they couldn't show their world-class potential.

"I still think that Chelsea came out motivated today and also played with intensity. I just checked the physical data, they were there with higher physical intensity than in their last games, but we still have outperformed them.

"It's important in this period of the season to collect points. It gives us more confidence but we travelled here with confidence and belief that it would be possible to give such a dominant performance.

"I can't wait to be on the sofa with coffee and cake and to watch this game back."

articles.body:
A University of Miami fan drew the attention of ESPN College GameDay on Saturday with a funny sign referencing the newly released Grand Theft Auto VI video game.

The sign, which was posted on College GameDay 's official X account, read, "I left Lucia to be here."

Lucia is one of the main, playable characters in GTA VI, and she has been the subject of many internet memes since the game was officially released on Thursday.

Given that GTA VI is set in Vice City, which is essentially a fictionalized version of Miami, the sign was a great fit for Saturday's ACC college football clash between No. 7 Miami and Virginia Tech.

articles.title: Bournemouth 2-0 Nottingham Forest: Evanilson on target again as Cherries make history with comfortable Premier League victory
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Bournemouth beat Nottingham Forest for their ninth successive victory in all competitions; Evanilson scored in his sixth Premier League game in a row; Justin Kluivert added a second; Alex Scott made his return from injury in the second half
articles.body:
It was a club-record ninth successive win in all competitions and the first time they have won five in a row in the Premier League. They have kept seven clean sheets in those games as well - only conceding against Ipswich in the league - with 23 goals scored.

A large part of that has been down to the form of Evanilson, and the Brazilian did not disappoint. He struck first with a wonderful effort - set up by the deftest of headers from James Hill - to extend his scoring run to six straight Premier League games.

It was a simple but effective break for Bournemouth's second as Forest failed to follow up a big win against Manchester City before the international break.

Marcus Tavernier sped down the left-hand side, with only Justin Kluivert for support. That was all he needed, though, as his low cross was turned home by the Netherlands international.

Bournemouth drew a number of fine saves from Matz Sels in the second half, although perhaps the brightest moment was the return of Alex Scott from injury. It was his first Cherries appearance since September 20 and his first overall game since October 3, when he played for England against Croatia.

He was part of a triple change in the 69th minute and from then on, Forest had the better of the play. However, they did little with it and could only muster one shot on target, despite have just one fewer shot than the Cherries (18).

The win sends Bournemouth into the top four ahead of the remaining games this weekend. Nottingham Forest slip down into 17th and are outside the relegation spots on goal difference.

3: GOOD STOP! Evanilson's his shot is stopped well by Sels at the near post.

18: GOAL! Evanilson finds the net with a one touch and finish past the goalkeeper.

45+2: GOAL! Kluivert finishes Tavernier's break with Bournemouth's second on the stroke of half-time.

67: SAVE! Kluivert strikes from the top of the box, but Sels stretches to send it over.

69: SUB! Bournemouth make a triple change with Scott returning to action for the first time in seven weeks.

86: SAVE! Sels again as Rayan fires straight at him.

Rose: We were relentless - a deserved win

Bournemouth head coach Marco Rose: "Really good [performance], especially in the first half. We knew that it's going to be difficult against a tough opponent, quite compact, consistent in everything they do.

"It's hard to create chances, but we did it. We created chances, we scored goals and we were relentless. We defended our goal at the end... with a deserved win.

"We were good in box defending. We never struggled really, we suffered, but we never struggled. It's an important part and phase of the game as well."

On Bournemouth's second goal: "It was the right moment, but if you're 2-0 up at half-time, it's always difficult if the opponent changed something and they did it.

"They brought [on] two new players, new energy and you could get in problems if you don't use the right approach for the second half, but we did it. We were ready and that's why it was a top performance. We enjoy this win, but Thursday [against Celta Vigo] we have to prove it again."

On Bournemouth's impressive defensive record: "This is the foundation for everything that we are - a hard-working team out of possession and that we do it together.

"Then we win balls, we score simple goals out of ball wins. And on the other side, we score goals from set-pieces. So we are unpredictable - and that's good."

Glasner: We're struggling to match physicality and intensity of PL opponents

Nottingham Forest head coach Oliver Glasner:

"We need to be more physical. We're struggling with the physicality, the intensity and the power these teams have. We have to improve because then we can stay in all these games.

"We had the same amount of shots most of the time, but this is the pattern and we never scored. We always conceded from a mistake and we all know especially in defence, you have to avoid mistakes because the Premier League is ruthless.

"In the attack again we try, but you also have to be ruthless because otherwise the Premier League will punish you.

"It was a very intense game from both sides, many long balls, many duels, many second balls. We have to accept that Bournemouth was a little bit better in these situations and that's why they won.

"First goal we lose the ball, second goal we lose the ball. We were well-organised behind the ball and I don't know why, but it happened and then we open the middle and this is where they score the goal.

"Especially the second goal straight before half-time, such an easy goal to give away. That hurts and then you can't win in the Premier League.

"For me today [Saturday] it was not the efficiency, it was that we made too many easy mistakes and Bournemouth took them."

articles.title: El Cádiz se estrena a domicilio, sale del barro y hunde al Sanse
articles.standfirst: Un golazo de Antoñito y los tantos de Izeta y Borja doblegan a una Real B que jugó casi toda la segunda parte con uno menos y acabó con nueve por las expulsiones de Marchal y Carrera
articles.summary: Un golazo de Antoñito y los tantos de Izeta y Borja doblegan a una Real B que jugó casi toda la segunda parte con uno menos y acabó con nueve por las expulsiones de Marchal y Carrera
articles.body: El Cádiz encontró en Zubieta una victoria de las que alivian y cambian el paisaje. Un golazo de Antoñito Cordero, que metió un derechazo por toda la escuadra, y los tantos postreros de Izeta y Borja Vázquez le sirven para doblegar a la Real Sociedad B, que jugó buena parte de la segunda parte con uno menos al ver Marchal dos tarjetas en apenas un minuto, y sumar así su primera victoria a domicilio. De este modo, los gaditanos vuelven a ganar cuatro jornadas después y salen provisionalmente de un descenso al que precisamente meten al Sanse, que ve truncada su racha de tres jornadas sumando y al final acabó con nueve por la expulsión de Carrera. Una tarde para olvidar para los de Ion Ansotegi, que además perderá a ambos jugadores para la próxima jornada. Los dos entrenadores movieron sus piezas de inicio. Ansotegi introdujo cambios en la Real B y Borja Jiménez agitó los laterales del Cádiz, con Gocholeishvili en la izquierda y Borja Vázquez en la derecha. También recuperó a Damián Rodríguez e Ibon Sánchez, mientras los jóvenes Noah Ukwuije y Manu Rivera continuaron en el centro de la defensa. Bajo la lluvia y el viento de Zubieta, los amarillos compitieron con seriedad y amenazaron pronto por medio de Antoñito Cordero, cuyo disparo salió rozando el larguero. El filial respondió con una gran ocasión de Gorka Carrera, que se plantó ante David Gil, pero se encontró con un Noah salvador. Mariezkurrena también rozó el gol antes de que Antoñito Cordero sacara la brocha justo antes de la pausa: recibió de Ibon Sánchez en la frontal y derechazo con efecto que se coló por la escuadra. Un golazo para mandar al Cádiz por delante al descanso. El propio Antoñito pudo ampliar la ventaja al regreso de los vestuarios, pero Olasagasti le ganó el duelo. Y apenas un minuto después llegó la acción que agitó el partido y que también puso la ración de polémica al encuentro. Saúl Ais mostró dos amarillas en apenas un minuto a Álex Marchal y dejó a la Real B con diez y, minutos después, señaló un penalti que, eso sí, fue corregido por el VAR por una mano de Gorosabel. Pese a estar con diez apretó la escuadra donostiarra y de hecho rondó el empate, pero primero Mariezkurrena no acertó tras una buena dejada de Dani Díaz y después el disparo con mucho efecto del propio Dani salió rozando el poste. Mientras, el Cádiz controlaba sin grandes apuros, pero tuvo que esperar hasta la recta final para respirar del todo, cuando Izeta soltó un zurdazo fuerte y raso para hacer el segundo tras gran recorte ante Kita dentro del área. Ya en el minuto 90 Borja Vázquez, tras un gran pase de Antoñito, remató la goleada y Gorka Carrera acabó expulsado en el último minuto. De esta forma, el Cádiz suma cuatro puntos en sus dos visitas consecutivas al País Vasco y sale del descenso para meter en él a la Real Sociedad B.

articles.title: Lincoln 0-1 Wrexham: George Thomason nets winner for Red Dragons
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Lincoln City and Wrexham at the ProAmpac Stadium on Saturday; George Thomason scores the only goal as Red Dragons claim a narrow late victory.
articles.body:
It was a game lacking real quality in the final third at Sincil Bank.

But Thomason kept his cool when the moment arose to fire Wrexham to victory with his 82nd-minute strike.

It was a first away league victory for Phil Parkinson's charges since the start of September when they beat Millwall 2-0.

The Red Dragons have now gone three games without defeat and will be hoping to use their recent upturn in form as a catalyst towards their play-off push.

For Lincoln, it was the latest bump in the road as the reality of being minnows in the Championship is really beginning to hit home.

Any hopes the international break would bring about a change in fortunes were dashed with a fourth loss on the spin, whilst it is their seventh defeat in nine.

Their only victory in that time was the 4-1 hammering of relegation rivals Burnley, which led to Nicky Hayen's sacking.

The first real chance of the contest fell to the visitors as Callum Doyle nodded wide of the mark from Thomason's delivery into the box.

Down the other end, Rob Street saw his own header well kept out by stopper Anthony Patterson.

Defender Demi Elerewe produced a great double block when he prevented Ollie Rathbone from breaking the deadlock.

Patterson was then called into action once more to deny Adam Reach's effort on the half hour mark after good link up play between Reach and Dan Oyegoke.

Street came close to changing the complexion of the respective half-time team talks when he agonisingly fired wide on the stroke of the break.

The second half was a poorer showing than the first with meaningful chances at a premium after the restart.

George Wickens got down low to keep out Rathbone's tame strike from outside the box in a routine bit of keeping.

Patterson barely had to move to stop Andrei Coubis' effort down the middle of his goal.

Dom Jefferies' free-kick did not threaten the visitors, whilst Oyegoke was kept out by another routine Patterson stop heading into the final quarter of an hour.

But the door was eventually unlocked when Thomason snatched the winner with eight minutes to go.

The 25-year-old pounced on a poor back pass and easily slotted home a left-footed effort beyond the on-rushing Wickens for his second goal of the campaign and most importantly to secure the points for the Welsh outfit.

Lincoln chucked on reinforcements to try and salvage something from the game.

Bailey Cadamarteri was denied Wrexham's second, with Patterson keeping out Jefferies right at the end.

"It's a very disappointing outcome. I thought we went toe-to-toe with Wrexham on the whole.

"The result has been decided by an error. It will be big learning for us as a group. We were trying to force the game, try to find a way to win it and unfortunately we've come away with zero points.

"The feel leading up to the goal, we got a bit too comfortable with the ball. A few passes went a little bit off script. We were perhaps irresponsible at times.

"But the people, the players, the group involved will learn really quickly that you can't indulge at any moment at this level and we got punished.

"Our performance as a whole was competitive enough. We were just starting to tip a nothing game, but unfortunately it's a really tough lesson for us all to learn.

"We looked physically good, but we just didn't quite connect around the penalty area.

"The game was there for us if we really wanted, but when we got that flow we made a big mistake and that sums it up."

"As any win, it's a huge one. We stood strong as a team. There was a group understanding of what was required.

"I spoke to the lads on Monday about the importance about getting our away form back on track.

"You can never guarantee a result, but the performance and the determination of the group…the supporters could see that.

"When the moment came, Thommo took it brilliant. But the defending is as important as that goal.

"I think we're targeting performances on a weekly basis. Each game is different and you need different qualities every game.

"Each win is so hard. It was great to celebrate with our supporters at the end. The players are pleased with that one.

"The lads who have got the shirts at the moment are putting in a great shift. We've had injury problems before, we've pieced teams together at a lot of levels. It's about being in a good position when those players come back.

"We've got good heart and good leadership in this team."

articles.title: Copete saca al Valencia del descenso
articles.standfirst: Un gol del defensa y las paradas de Dimitrievski anulan el efecto Vallecas
articles.summary: Un gol del defensa y las paradas de Dimitrievski anulan el efecto Vallecas
articles.body: El Valencia se armó de pico y pala para extraer una victoria de oro de Vallecas. Su tercer triunfo, los tres a domicilio, le permiten salir momentáneamente de los puestos de descenso a la espera de otros resultados de la jornada. Fue Copete, titular tras nueve meses de lesión, el que anotó un tanto que vale tres puntos. El trabajo defensivo de Aguirre empieza a hacer efecto. Porque el Rayo, bastante sólido como local todo el curso, gozó de buenas ocasiones, pero se topó ante Dimitrievski en los momentos clave. Aguirre encontró en Maffeo y Rioja la pareja que tenía que equilibrar su banda izquierda, al no poder contar con Gayá ni Jesús Vázquez. Además, horas antes del partido, Arnaut Danjuma había abandonado la convocatoria por la muerte de su padre. Y la clave era evitar que Ratiu ni Unai López -o De Frutos o Isi- encontraran facilidades para meter centros desde ese costado. La movilidad de los tres mediapuntas locales sacó de sitio en más de una ocasión a la defensa visitante en la que se multiplicaban las coberturas de Tárrega y Copete, que cuajaron un gran partido. En el intercambio de posiciones ofensivas rayistas brotaron las mejores ocasiones del equipo local desde las botas de De Frutos. Primero por colocación y después, por puros reflejos para sacar el brazo y desviar el disparo, Dimitrievski sostenía a su equipo en los peores momentos. Si el Valencia aparecía en el área de Emil Audero solía ser por intervención de Dani Raba. Escorado a la derecha, el jugador cántabro, que desequilibraba por fuera y por dentro, reclamó penalti de Mujaid, con la mano muy abajo y casi pegada al cuerpo. El Valencia necesitó un disparo a puerta para adelantarse en el marcador. Copete, desde el punto de penalti, colocó de cabeza a gol un saque de esquina botado por Guerra. Y con esa ventaja mínima el partido se fue al descanso. El Rayo arrancó enérgico la segunda parte. Y a punto estuvo de Unai López de provocar un penalti de Raba, con media bota pisando la línea en el momento de trabarlo. La falta, que no penalti, a punto estuvo de convertirla Lejeune –que tiene variedades ofensivas para dar y regalar- con un potente disparo que rozó la escuadra. Con el equipo local centrifugando el juego, el Valencia pudo aumentar la distancia. Marcó Raba, pero había fuera de juego previo de Rioja. Y Copete casi anotó de cabeza otra vez tras un saque de falta de Raba. El Valencia se encerró, más por el empuje del rival que por voluntad propia, y Unai López enganchó un trallazo lejanísimo que se estrelló en la escuadra de la portería de Dimitrievski. El Rayo arrinconó al Valencia en su campo, pero le faltó lucidez y acierto para lograr al menos un punto.

Ahead of the highly anticipated Army-Navy college football rivalry game on Dec. 12, Army pranked Navy on Saturday.

The upper-deck seats that usually spell out "Go Navy" at Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium in Annapolis, Maryland, were re-arranged to spell "Go Army."

Per Chris Vannini of The Athletic, security footage captured in-uniform Army cadets sneaking into the stadium at around 1 a.m. ET on Saturday morning before leaving at 4 a.m. ET.

articles.title: Fifpro criticises Bayern Munich for Jamal Musiala comments
articles.summary: Football players' union Fifpro says it is concerned by German club Bayern Munich's comments about Jamal Musiala's contract.
articles.body:
Football players' union Fifpro says it is concerned by comments from Bayern Munich's hierarchy about Jamal Musiala's contract, adding the German club "should know better".

Musiala collapsed twice in four days during pre-season and the 23-year-old Germany international said he had been diagnosed with "easily treatable absence seizures, which are due to a neurological dysfunction".

Bayern honorary president Uli Hoeness said earlier this month Musiala may never "regain the performance level he once had" .

The Bundesliga club's chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen has also questioned , external the lucrative contract extension the forward signed in 2025, running until 2030, if Musiala fails to get back to his best form, while his predecessor Karl-Heinz Rummenigge has suggested , external the deal may need to be renegotiated.

"Bayern's honorary president, chief executive and former chief executive have all publicly questioned Musiala's contract in quick succession," said a Fifpro statement. , external

"In Fifpro's view, this is a co-ordinated strategy to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives ahead of any negotiations. A club of Bayern's standing should know better."

Musiala may never return to his best - Hoeness

Two collapses in four days - what's happening to Musiala?

Musiala, who joined Bayern in 2019 after coming through Chelsea's academy, came on for the German champions after 70 minutes in a 1-1 draw with Cologne on Friday as he made his first outing since scoring in a 7-0 win against Union Berlin on 18 September.

He has made five appearances for the club this season, scoring two goals and providing one assist.

"Bayern has a duty of care to Musiala," added Fifpro. "Across professional football, uncertainty about a player's future can take a toll on their mental health, particularly when they are recovering from injury.

"Making Musiala's health and future a matter of public debate adds to that pressure. Any concerns about his contract should be raised privately with him and his representatives.

"Contracts are there to be respected. An injury or a dip in form gives a club no grounds to reopen terms it agreed to, just as a run of outstanding performances gives a player no automatic right to a pay rise."

Musiala's return to the Bayern side came in the same game in which England striker Harry Kane suffered an ankle injury and was subsequently ruled out "for the next few months".

articles.title: Aguirre bromea con el trabajo defensivo de sus jugadores: "No hicieron caso los cabrones, nos tiraron 200 centros"
articles.standfirst: El técnico del Valencia se va feliz tras la victoria contra el Rayo, aunque es sincero: "Nos pudieron empatar"
articles.summary: El técnico del Valencia se va feliz tras la victoria contra el Rayo, aunque es sincero: "Nos pudieron empatar"
articles.body: Javier Aguirre se marchó satisfecho de Vallecas tras una victoria que calificó de "importante" para reforzar la confianza de un Valencia que sigue sumando en su lucha por escalar posiciones, aunque admitió que el triunfo llegó tras un ejercicio de resistencia en una segunda parte en la que el Rayo estuvo cerca de evitar la derrota. El técnico destacó el esfuerzo colectivo de sus jugadores en defensa para contener el juego exterior del conjunto madrileño, aunque, fiel a su estilo directo, bromeó al reconocer que sus futbolistas no siguieron del todo las consignas para frenar los numerosos centros al área, como había advertido en la previa. Además, elogió el regreso goleador de Copete después de nueve meses de ausencia por lesión y lanzó un mensaje de optimismo de cara al próximo compromiso en Mestalla, donde espera brindar a la afición la primera gran alegría de la temporada en casa ante Osasuna. ¿Qué importancia tiene esta victoria para el equipo, especialmente en el aspecto anímico? "Son tres puntos importantes, sobre todo por la parte anímica y moral. Es evidente que las victorias traen alegría y un impulso anímico importante. Seguimos sufriendo, está claro. Hoy pudimos haber empatado fácilmente. Tuvimos una defensa bastante baja en la segunda parte, heroica diría yo, y ellos nos apretaron mucho. Es un equipo que trata bien la pelota y que tira muchos centros; es el segundo equipo de la Liga que más centros realiza. Sabíamos eso y metimos gente alta para que no nos hicieran daño, pero ellos son muy capaces. Fue una victoria sufrida y, por lo menos, hoy estaremos contentos". ¿Qué valoración hace del trabajo defensivo y de las ayudas a los laterales? "No hicieron caso los cabrones, porque nos tiraron 200 centros, así que parece que no sirvió de mucho el comentario. Bueno, la parte defensiva y el trabajo en equipo fueron importantes hoy. Nunca tuvieron superioridad por fuera, no consiguieron situaciones de tres contra dos ni de dos contra uno. Siempre seguimos sus movimientos y paredes. Insisto, son muy capaces y nos pusieron muchísimos centros, pero en ese aspecto me quedo tranquilo. Fueron muy buenos y nosotros hicimos lo que pudimos, sin dejar de trabajar para defender esos centros". ¿Qué supone el gol de Copete después de nueve meses de lesión? "José es un jugador especial. El día de la Copa, me atrevo a hacer público esto, dijo unas palabras muy bonitas. Después de nueve meses, hizo alusión a un compañero que también llevaba mucho tiempo en su lugar y nos llegó al corazón aquel día. Hoy José ha vuelto a demostrar lo que es: te da todo lo que tiene, no se guarda nada. Hasta el final tuvimos que sustituirlo porque había hecho un desgaste físico importante. Llevaba mucho tiempo esperando este momento". ¿Qué mensaje le manda a la afición de cara al próximo partido en Mestalla contra Osasuna? "Mucho cariño. A ver si le damos una alegría en casa. No hemos podido hacerlo hasta ahora, la verdad es que han sido partidos complicados: Bilbao, Villarreal y Real Madrid. A ver si esta vez se nos da. Vamos a competir, eso es evidente, y ellos también. Ojalá demos una alegría en casa a la gente".

articles.title: El grupo dueño de Atlético Nacional desembarca en América de Cali y sacude el fútbol colombiano
articles.standfirst: Organización Ardila Lülle llega al América de Cali: qué implica la alianza con dueños de Nacional
articles.summary: Organización Ardila Lülle llega al América de Cali: qué implica la alianza con dueños de Nacional
articles.body: La noticia que encendió el debate en el fútbol profesional colombiano (FPC) —y que titulares como el de Semana resumieron en torno a la llegada de la Organización Ardila Lülle al América de Cali— tiene como eje concreto un acuerdo de patrocinio oficial entre Postobón y el conjunto escarlata, anunciado el viernes 20 de noviembre de 2026. Aunque algunos titulares sugieren a primera vista una compra o toma de control societario similar a la de Atlético Nacional, el acuerdo corresponde a una alianza comercial de patrocinio de largo plazo, vigente hasta 2029, que vincula directamente a una de las empresas insignia del conglomerado con el club vallecaucano en un momento clave de su historia. De acuerdo con el anuncio oficial realizado por América de Cali el 20 de noviembre de 2026, Postobón se convierte en patrocinador oficial del club desde lo que resta de 2026 y durante los años calendario 2027, 2028 y 2029. El alcance del convenio es amplio y abarca distintas estructuras de la institución: Equipos profesionales y formativos: cobija tanto al plantel profesional masculino como al femenino, además de las divisiones menores y categorías formativas del club. Presencia en la camiseta: la marca aparecerá en la camiseta oficial —en la zona de la clavícula en los equipos profesionales y en el pecho en las categorías de formación—, con exclusividad definida dentro de la categoría de bebidas no alcohólicas. Activaciones y hospitalidad: el acuerdo incluye derechos de uso de marca, activaciones comerciales, visibilidad, pauta digital y experiencias en programas de hospitalidad para conectar con la afición. Acompañamiento al centenario: el vínculo cubrirá de lleno 2027, año en que América de Cali celebra su centenario institucional. Por ahora, ni el club ni la compañía han hecho público el monto económico exacto ni los detalles financieros específicos del contrato. Uno de los puntos que más ruido genera entre los hinchas y analistas del FPC es la relación entre Postobón, la Organización Ardila Lülle y Atlético Nacional. El anuncio confirma que Postobón entra como patrocinador comercial hasta 2029, no que la Organización Ardila Lülle haya comprado la ficha mayoritaria del cuadro escarlata, donde el entorno de Tulio Gómez ha sido señalado públicamente como el actor mayoritario que ha buscado socios o inversionistas de cara al centenario. Que una marca emblema de la Organización Ardila Lülle estampe su nombre en la camiseta del América de Cali no pasa desapercibido en el ecosistema del FPC por varias razones: Simbolismo en un país futbolero polarizado: el choque de camisetas, rivalidades históricas y la memoria de grandes disputas deportivas y empresariales en Colombia hacen que cualquier acercamiento comercial entre marcas ligadas a Atlético Nacional y uno de sus grandes rivales históricos genere reacciones inmediatas en redes sociales y gradas. El camino al centenario escarlata (2027): llegar a los cien años de existencia exige músculo comercial, visibilidad y respaldo de marca. Contar con un socio de alcance nacional como Postobón fortalece la vitrina del club en un año de alta carga simbólica. Un contexto deportivo y financiero exigente: el anuncio llega en medio de un calendario de alta tensión para América de Cali —con participación en los cuadrangulares de la Liga BetPlay 2026-II y la final de la Copa BetPlay— y en un momento en el que la situación financiera y los compromisos laborales del club han sido tema de debate público. A partir de este acuerdo hasta 2029, la atención del entorno futbolístico se concentrará en tres frentes: cómo se materializan las activaciones y la presencia de Postobón en las distintas divisiones del club, qué impacto real tiene este respaldo en el flujo de caja y la proyección comercial del América rumbo a su centenario en 2027, y cómo evoluciona el panorama de posibles inversionistas o reestructuración del equipo en los próximos meses.

articles.title: Imga, primera baja de España en el Mundial
articles.standfirst: El extremo del Athletic sufre una lesión en los isquiotibiales y regresará a España para iniciar su recuperación. Cubillo no podrá incorporar a ningún sustituto
articles.summary: El extremo del Athletic sufre una lesión en los isquiotibiales y regresará a España para iniciar su recuperación. Cubillo no podrá incorporar a ningún sustituto
articles.body: Malas noticias para España en el Mundial Sub-17 de Catar. Christian Imga se convierte en la primera baja de la selección de David Cubillo. El extremo del Athletic sufrió una lesión en los isquiotibiales durante el estreno ante China (5-0) y tendrá que abandonar la concentración para regresar a España, donde comenzará su proceso de recuperación. Los peores presagios se confirmaron al día siguiente del encuentro. Las pruebas realizadas al futbolista apuntan a un periodo de baja de entre cuatro y cinco semanas, por lo que se perderá lo que resta de campeonato. Un contratiempo importante para el jugador, afectado por una lesión que pone fin de manera prematura a su primera experiencia mundialista. La baja también supone un problema para David Cubillo, que tendrá que afrontar el resto del torneo con 20 futbolistas. La normativa de la FIFA no permite sustituir a jugadores lesionados una vez iniciada la competición, salvo en el caso de los porteros. Por tanto, España no podrá incorporar a un nuevo futbolista para cubrir la ausencia del atacante rojiblanco. El seleccionador pierde así una de sus alternativas para el extremo izquierdo, posición en la que Imga fue titular frente a China. Cubillo deberá reorganizar sus opciones ofensivas, con Iu Martínez y Rafa Cruz como posibles recambios para ocupar esa demarcación. Una baja sensible para España después de un estreno que había dejado grandes sensaciones sobre el césped.

articles.title: Malen 'rompe' la Serie A: 16 goles en 15 partidos para comandar a una gran Roma
articles.standfirst: 'Póker' del neerlandés ante el Parma en el Tardini
articles.summary: 'Póker' del neerlandés ante el Parma en el Tardini
articles.body: Los datos no mienten: los dos equipos de Roma nunca habían estado tan bien a estas alturas de una temporada en Italia. Y una jornada más, ambos están invictos. Si la Lazio venció al Lecce en casa (3-0), la Roma goleó en el Tardini al Parma (1-5). Los de Gasperini se colocan segundos, a la espera de lo que haga el Inter en Bérgamo, gracias al 'póker' de goles de un estelar Donyell Malen. Ya antes de arrancar el partido, la Roma sonreía. Y es que tras el parón, Gasperini recuperaba nombres clave como Svilar o Paulo Dybala. Y eso, después de la larga baja de ambos, era mucho decir. Fue precisamente 'La Joya' el que empezó a construir el 0-1 aunque la asistencia contó para Lulli. Malen, sea como fuere, controló de forma espectacular dentro del área y se inventó un golazo. El empate del Parma, ya en la segunda parte, quedó en anécdota: una buena contra finalizada por Elphege que resultó insuficente. 'La Loba' se desquitó en tres minutos y, a falta de 20, sentenciaba el partido. Primero Malen, para hacer doblete en esos instantes; después, el joven y talentoso Rodrigo Mora. Pero el MVP de la tarde en Parma fue, sin duda alguna, Donyell Malen. El neerlandés, que no había anotado en la última fecha (pero sí dado dos asistencias), cerró su gran partido con dos goles más: el 1-4 y el 1-5. Un 'póker' de goles de '10' que lo coloca con 12 goles en 11 partidos de Serie A... y otros cuatro en cuatro encuentros de Champions. 16 en 15, en total. Casi nada.

articles.title: Chelsea 1-4 Leeds: Xabi Alonso's honeymoon period appears to be over
articles.summary: The honeymoon period is over for Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso, who is now in firefighting mode after a 4-1 defeat by Leeds at Stamford Bridge.
articles.body:
Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso is already in firefighting mode.

His team were booed by their own supporters at several points during a dominant 4-1 Leeds victory at Stamford Bridge, their first win there since 1999.

The first negative reaction came at half-time while the score was still 1-1. The ground then began to empty after the third and fourth Leeds goals, and the fans remaining voiced their dissent once more at the final whistle.

Although there were mitigating circumstances, including a potentially harsh penalty decision against them and the loss of midfielder Moises Caicedo to injury, joining a five-strong list of players on the treatment table, the defeat was thoroughly deserved.

It leaves Chelsea with three losses in their past four Premier League matches and they have slipped from fifth place to eighth, already 14 points behind league leaders Arsenal .

In October, Tottenham won at Stamford Bridge for only the second time in the Premier League era, while the 1-0 defeat at bottom club Sunderland before the international break was another alarm bell.

It is the first time since 1967 that Chelsea have lost at home to both Leeds and Spurs in the same season.

"We need to find solutions, for sure, because there will be setbacks during any game," Alonso said after the match.

"To be able to go through that and to know that it's still so long to play, it's something mandatory in this competition and today I felt that probably we are in a fragile moment mentally.

"When we received a punch we didn't recover that strongly."

Okafor double delivers rare win for Leeds at Chelsea

'Officials can't use common sense' - was Rogers handball correct?

Indeed, even when Chelsea have been winning matches, they have often looked unconvincing.

Yet Blues supporters chanted their new manager's name and seemed optimistic after the summer transfer business - despite a disappointing 10th-place finish last season.

Club record £117m signing Morgan Rogers was joined by the experienced trio of Emiliano Martinez, Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson.

It was the clinical finishing of Rogers, along with Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro earlier in the season, that masked the underlying fragility of Alonso's team.

Before this weekend, the Blues ranked 14th for expected goal difference and were joint 12th in Opta's expected points table.

After their latest setback, ex-England forward and BBC Match of the Day pundit Alan Shearer said: " Chelsea were all over the place. Once Moises Caicedo went off injured early on, there was no physicality and they looked weak.

"They hardly created anything going forward and the back four didn't look comfortable. There was no desire, cohesion or fight from the home side, but we shouldn't take anything away from Leeds .

"Two weeks ago Chelsea were bullied by Sunderland centre-forward Brian Brobbey and they let Dominic Calvert-Lewin do the same today, which is alarming.

"It's fair to say Xabi Alonso's honeymoon period is over. He needs to tell his players this simply isn't good enough. They are miles off it and have to do better in every department."

In Alonso's defence, Chelsea had problems before his arrival.

They finished 10th last season, having been outrun in 37 of their 38 matches, and had three managers during a chaotic campaign.

Remarkably, Chelsea have seven more points from corresponding fixtures this season and last, but it mostly serves to show how low the bar was set.

Champions League qualification was again the club's pre-season target and Alonso's appointment was designed to bring stability and authority.

The former Real Madrid and Liverpool midfielder had an impressive playing career and earned much early admiration as a manager, guiding Bayer Leverkusen to a league and cup double in 2024.

However, the Spaniard, who was sacked by Real Madrid last season, has yet to establish any real consistency - beyond his defence leaking goals regularly.

Only Crystal Palace , Coventry City and Ipswich Town have conceded more goals than Chelsea this season.

Chelsea are also now averaging fewer than a goal per game since Joao Pedro suffered a thigh injury in training. Alongside Pedro and now Caicedo, Jorrel Hato, Maxence Lacroix, Reece James and Jamie Gittens are also injured.

It highlights how they have gained little benefit of having a season without European football.

Alonso is also beginning to face criticism from sections of the fanbase for both his team selections and substitutions.

Chief among the reasons is the constant chopping and changing of the starting XI, having now made 28 line-up changes (behind only Tottenham ) while also switching between back-four and back-three systems.

In addition, Alonso is being criticised for his use of personnel, having deployed Pedro Neto as a striker on two occasions and, some would argue, not made enough use of exciting young winger Estevao.

Against Leeds he gave striker Emmanuel Emegha his first start alongside Estevao and, although the Dutch striker scored, the pair were the first players he substituted while Chelsea were chasing the game at 3-1 down.

Similarly, his late in-game interventions are under scrutiny, including the decision to bring on striker Welbeck only in the 90th minute of the defeat by Spurs .

He took until the 64th minute to make changes against Leeds when Chelsea were already 3-1 down. Only three clubs had made more substitutions in the last 15 minutes than Chelsea in the league this season.

Given Leeds ' strengths, Chelsea should have been better prepared for what was coming. Before kick-off, Leeds had applied more high-intensity pressures in the opposition half than any other team in the Premier League.

They had also generated the most expected goals from set-pieces and won the most duels. Leeds maintained those trends at Stamford Bridge against a Chelsea side often accused of being soft.

Chelsea have had problems in recent seasons, but this was still their worst home defeat since a 4-1 loss to Brentford in 2022.

Likewise, it is almost uncharted territory in Alonso's managerial career, having only previously lost at home by a three-goal margin once.

The stadium emptied and supporters again left early.

Players displayed negative body language and argued with one another both during the match and after the final whistle.

As a result, Alonso has gone from needing to fix defensive issues to dealing with problems that appear to be spreading throughout the squad.

articles.title: Newcastle 2-2 Arsenal: Player ratings for Premier League draw
articles.summary: BBC Sport's Alex Howell shares his player ratings for Newcastle and Arsenal's 2-2 draw in the Premier League - and you can rate the players too.
articles.body:
Arsenal and Newcastle played out an entertaining 2-2 draw at St James' Park on Saturday.

The Gunners took the lead through Eberechi Eze in the first half before Harvey Barnes equalised after the break.

The hosts went ahead when Malick Thiaw bundled in from a corner before Noni Madueke brought the Gunners level with an excellent strike, and that is how it finished.

BBC Sport's Alex Howell has rated the players - and you can have your say too.

What do BBC Sport's player ratings mean?

Lukas Hornicek: His kicking was slightly erratic. Nearly got caught on the ball by Kai Havertz after taking too long to release it. Could have done better with the second Arsenal goal. 5

Amar Dedic : Booked after pulling back Eberechi Eze and had a tough evening against the England forward. 5

Malick Thiaw: Scored the goal to put Newcastle in front, which capped an excellent performance in central defence. 8

Dan Burn: Some crucial clearances in the first half and played a big part as Newcastle took the lead. 7

Lewis Hall: A big error for the opening goal when he failed to deal with a clipped ball over the top. The left back redeemed himself with a crucial block to deny Noni Madueke and provided some excellent deliveries into the Arsenal box. 7

Sean Steur: Showed quality on the ball and a calmness you do not often see in an 18-year-old, but taken off at half time. 6

Lewis Miley: Quality on the ball and worked well with Steur. Was the deepest of the Newcastle midfield in the second half. 7

Jacob Murphy: An early shot and tried to catch David Raya off his line, but also taken off at the break after a quiet first half. 5

Joe Willock: An all-action performance and his physicality was a big reason why Newcastle improved in the second half. 7

Harvey Barnes: An excellent finish to bring Newcastle level and was always direct. 8

William Osula: Isolated as he led the Newcastle attack but did very well to assist his side's opening goal. 7

Tino Livramento (on 46, Dedic): Made a huge impact after coming on at half-time. 7

Anthony Elanga (on 46, Murphy): His pace meant Newcastle always had an option in behind. 6

Jacob Ramsey (on 46, Steur): Added drive to the midfield. 7

Subs not used: Pope, Schar, Gonzalez, Wissa, Fernandez-Pardo.

David Raya: Was taken off with what looked like a serious shoulder problem after conceding twice. 5

Jurrien Timber: Arsenal used the Dutchman's aerial ability to get up the pitch quickly. Picked up some dangerous positions when the Gunners had the ball. 6

Ezri Konsa: The centre-back looked to be cruising before Arsenal conceded twice in the second half. 6

Gabriel Magalhaes: Got caught up in a battle with Osula as Arsenal conceded a second to go behind. 6

Riccardo Calafiori: A quieter attacking display than usual from the marauding left-back. 6

Declan Rice: Started the game very well but could not stop the Newcastle turnaround . 7

Martin Odegaard: An uncharacteristic mistake to gift Newcastle a way back into the match, but then made amends by setting up Madueke. 6

Eberechi Eze: Scored the opening goal of the game with a powerful finish. Looked sharp and provided an outlet. 7

Noni Madueke: Lots of positive moments from the winger and scored a great goal to bring Arsenal level. A consistent threat. 8

articles.title: Uno a uno del Real Madrid contra el Celta: valoración y comentarios
articles.standfirst: Análisis de la actuación de los jugadores y de Mourinho
articles.summary: Análisis de la actuación de los jugadores y de Mourinho
articles.body: El Madrid vuelve a la competición ante el Celta con pocos cambios respecto al último once ante el Valencia. Los dos laterales, Trent y Carreras, más Camavinga, son las tres novedades de Mourinho en el equipo inicial. Vinicius, pese a volver a la Liga tras cumplir sanción, arranca desde el banquillo ante el impulso de Diomande, que se mantiene como titular. PRIMERA PARTE: No puede hacer nada en el gol del Celta, con Pablo Durán rematando a placer. Atrapa abajo otro disparo del atacante celeste. PRIMERA PARTE: Demasiado cerrado en la jugada del gol del Celta, teniendo que recorrer mucha distancia para tapar la incursión de Javi Galán. Centro fallido en una buena posición para llevar peligro. Otro mal pase en una posición buenísima para poner un balón peligroso por delante de la defensa. PRIMERA PARTE: Aguanta muy bien un mano a mano con Williot muy peligroso, forzando el tiro erróneo del celeste. PRIMERA PARTE: Muy atento y sin concesiones en los duelos con Pablo Durán. PRIMERA PARTE: Intentando proyectarse en ataque y sin sufrir en defensa. PRIMERA PARTE: Llega tarde a la ayuda para cerrar el remate de Pablo Durán en el primer gol del Celta. PRIMERA PARTE: No llega a cabecear en condiciones un gran centro de Diomande desde la banda en la primera ocasión madridista. PRIMERA PARTE:. Pidió un penalti en una acción con Pablo Durán. Buena acción individual, pero se precipita en la definición con un mal disparo teniendo más alternativas. Disparo desde fuera del área que se le marcha alto. PRIMERA PARTE: Destellos de calidad en arrancadas en conducción marca de la casa con las que intentó desequilibrar.
