articles.body: El PSV no falló en su visita al campo del NEC Nijmegen y será, una semana más, líder de la Eredivisie... en la previa de su viaje al Bernabéu para jugar la Champions League. Aprovechó, además, la derrota del Feyenoord para aumentar su ventaja a cuatro puntos sobre los de Róterdam. El Ajax, que juega mañana, podría ser segundo si se impone. Para el PSV fue un paseo: al descanso ya ganaba 0-3. Kostic, Perisic, Kaplan en propia puerta y Ruben van Bommel, hijo de Mark, hicieron los goles para el equipo de Peter Bosz. Aun así, hubo grietas en defensa y Kovar, con siete paradas, fue uno de los mejores del equipo de Eindhoven. Es el tercer triunfo consecutivo en Eredivisie para un PSV que se confirma como el gran candidato a ganar, una vez más, la liga neerlandesa. Peor le fue a un Feyenoord que, contra todo pronostico, perdió en De Kuip ante el Excelsior. Y, de hecho, con remontada visitante. A los dos minutos ya ganaba El Feyenoord con un tanto de Read pero el Excelsior remontó antes del descanso con el español Mario Domínguez y Yegoian. En el segundo tiempo, Widell selló el triunfo.

Un sencillo pero emotivo homenaje con el que se recuerda al delantero del Tenerife, cuya trágica muerte conmocionó al fútbol español el pasado 3 de noviembre. El recuerdo del delantero continúa así presente en uno de los escenarios más emblemáticos del fútbol mundial, después de que todo el fútbol español se haya volcado con las muestras de cariño tras el trágico accidente. articles.title: Kike Salas hace justicia en el derbi
articles.standfirst: Antony adelantó al Betis pero el canterano igualó en el 91' con la ayuda de Álvaro Valles
articles.summary: Antony adelantó al Betis pero el canterano igualó en el 91' con la ayuda de Álvaro Valles
articles.body: Como Rómulo y Remo, dos hermanos de una misma ciudad se enfrentaron esta tarde en el Sánchez-Pizjuán. Comparten origen, calles y memoria, pero cuando el balón echa a rodar, solo hay sitio para uno. Tablas en el primer duelo cainita de la temporada. Kike Salas premió el empuje de un Sevilla que compitió hasta el último momento, pero pecó de falta de acierto. El Betis, sin hacer un gran partido, no se arrugó y esperó su momento. Antony adelantó a los suyos en la segunda mitad. Ahora toca esperar algo menos de tres meses para devolver la visita en La Cartuja. Otro capítulo de la misma historia. Nervión colgó el 'no hay billetes' en un derbi con pocas sorpresas en las alineaciones. Guridi entró en detrimento de Kochorashvili y Aitor Ruibal ocupó el lugar de Parrott en el ataque verdiblanco En el Gol Norte, un mensaje: "Una historia de grandeza". También hubo recuerdo para Alfon y Carmona, con camisetas de apoyo tras las graves lesiones sufridas durante el parón de selecciones. Vamos al lío, que un Sevilla-Betis no da tregua. Tampoco Sánchez Martínez. El colegiado tenía el gatillo fácil y fue sacando tarjetas a la mínima, algunas sin sentido, al que protestaba y al banquillo, para rebajar las pulsaciones. Consiguió lo contrario. El anfitrión, intenso y fuerte al choque, estuvo un puntito por encima del vecino buscando la portería de Valles. Tuvo su momento con llegadas muy claras, pero mostró durante todo el partido una preocupante falta de acierto. Fofana probó fortuna con un lanzamiento directo de falta que se marchó por encima de la portería. Poco después, Félix Correia pudo adelantar al Sevilla tras una buena combinación por la derecha, pero su disparo se marchó demasiado cruzado. Otra más para la cuenta. Stassin puso un centro desde la derecha que atravesó el área pequeña sin encontrar rematador. Ni Félix ni Vargas llegaron a tiempo. Kike Salas tuvo que meter la cabeza para desviar un centro muy peligroso de Antony. El central, que ya había visto la amarilla por un codazo a Aitor Ruibal, obligó al catalán a lucir desde entonces un aparatoso vendaje en la cabeza. Antony, que estrenaba look quizá en busca de dejar atrás su mala racha, también reclamaba protagonismo en la banda: hacía señales al banquillo para pedir una pastilla contra las náuseas. El Sevilla no levantaba el pie. Tras un robo, Stassin se plantó en el área y buscó el disparo cruzado y raso, pero Valles respondió con una buena mano. Antony volvió a intentarlo, esta vez encarando hacia dentro, aunque su golpeo se marchó desviado. El brasileño estaba siendo el mejor del Betis y acabaría encontrando su premio. Pero sería más adelante. Kike Salas buscó la especialidad de la casa con un cabezazo que se marchó fuera y al que Guridi no pudo llegar. Bartra, impecable, cortó algún acercamiento más mientras el partido se acercaba al descanso. El Betis consiguió estirarse en los últimos compases y terminó durmiendo el balón durante el minuto de añadido. Todo quedaba pendiente para la segunda mitad. Sin cambios arrancó el segundo acto, aunque García Plaza ya daba instrucciones a Kochorashvili en el banquillo. El Betis mantenía su apuesta por sacar el balón jugado desde atrás, mientras el Sevilla apretaba con una presión alta. Y llegó el primero de la tarde. Antony, el más incisivo de los verdiblancos, recibió de Isco en la frontal, se perfiló y armó el disparo. La pelota acabó en el fondo de la red tras tocar en un defensor. Un gol con algo de fortuna, pero que premiaba al brasileño. El equipo de García Plaza no se arrugó, aunque pudo recibir un segundo golpe apenas unos minutos después. Abde puso el centro y el '7', completamente solo, conectó el remate. Odysseas se hizo enorme para evitar el segundo. El derbi no aflojó. Kike Salas pisó a Isco y el banquillo reclamó la segunda amarilla para el central. Poco después, el Sevilla pidió penalti sobre el canterano en una disputa por un balón aéreo. Ni una cosa ni la otra. Ambas acciones quedaron en nada. Más pólvora sobre el césped del Sánchez-Pizjuán. Isaac, Robbie Ure y Deossa entraron para agitar el partido. El Sevilla no estaba haciendo un mal encuentro, ni mucho menos, pero el fútbol tiene una ley que no entiende de merecimientos: el gol manda. Lo justo era, al menos, el empate y lo puso Kike Salas con un disparo que se comió Valles. Error grosero del verdiblanco, que está firmando una temporada sobresaliente. Antes había tenido tres el Sevilla, balón al palo incluido. Cada uno luchó con sus armas, pero la sensación es agridulce. El Sevilla, porque entiende que mereció más por las ocasiones que tuvo. El Betis protestó pidiendo la segunda amarilla de Kike Salas tras el mencionado pisotón a Isco. El crentral que, además, terminó siendo decisivo para los suyos. Reparto de puntos entre dos equipos que siguen en Europa y que dejan todo en el aire para la vuelta en La Cartuja. Porque el derbi se vive al margen de LaLiga. No son solo tres puntos.

articles.title: Nine wins in a row - Bournemouth & Evanilson continue to make history
articles.summary: With a ninth successive win, Bournemouth continue to make history under new manager Marco Rose.
articles.body:
"We have to stick together and face reality."

That is how Bournemouth manager Marco Rose responded after his side had dropped into the Premier League relegation zone with a 5-1 defeat by Chelsea.

Six weeks on, it is an entirely different story.

The Cherries are up to fourth in the top flight, having clinched a club record ninth successive win in all competitions - with five in the league.

It is a far cry from that thumping defeat at Stamford Bridge, which left Rose without a victory in his first six Premier League matches in charge.

Bournemouth earned just three points from those six games (draws against Everton, Newcastle and Brentford - when the Cherries squandered winning positions) and fans may have been fearing the worst.

From the outside looking in, it seemed as though the appointment of Rose might not deliver the fortunes that had been expected.

The 50-year-old, who accepted the unenviable task of succeeding Andoni Iraola, called for his side to take "responsibility" after the defeat by Chelsea.

"Three points after six games, we need a reaction. Everyone has to take responsibility to do better," said Rose at the time.

"We knew it was going to be a demanding season. We have to stick together and face reality. The reality is we have three points after six games."

The Cherries have not only responded to Rose's rallying cry, they have exceeded all expectations.

Those nine straight wins include five in the league - and his side are now only four points behind second-placed Brighton.

After easing to a 2-0 victory against Nottingham Forest on Saturday, Rose said: "We don't think about records, we just think about the next game.

"We took the right approach. We knew it would be tough and we would have to stay patient, and that's what we did. It was a top performance and a deserved win."

'I will smile, not just because of the table - because we win'

Since arriving in England in July, Rose has come across as a composed presence, regardless of Bournemouth's results.

However, the former Borussia Dortmund and RB Leipzig manager was unable to hide his delight at his side's record-breaking victory against Forest.

Shortly after the full-time whistle sounded at the Vitality Stadium, Rose unleashed a series of celebratory fist pumps in front of the delighted home fans.

It was arguably the first time Rose had let down his guard since arriving on the South Coast four months ago - and who could blame him, given the significance of the result?

It is the first time in the club's history they have won five consecutive Premier League matches.

The prospect of securing European football for a second consecutive season is growing by the week.

In addition to wins over Sunderland, Manchester United, Leeds, Ipswich and Nottingham Forest in the Premier League, Bournemouth have beaten AC Milan in the Europa League and Aston Villa in the League Cup.

Their remarkable run of nine wins across all competitions surpasses their previous record of eight, achieved in both the 1998-99 and 2012-13 seasons.

Bournemouth are currently also second in the Europa League league phase and are one of only three teams to have won all four of their matches so far.

"Tonight I will smile, but not just because of the table - because we win," Rose told Match of the Day.

Meanwhile, Justin Kluivert - who scored Bournemouth's second goal against Forest - urged his team-mates to remain "humble" and "not settle for less" before upcoming matches against Celta Vigo and Fulham.

One of the main reasons behind Bournemouth's upturn in form has been the hot streak forward Evanilson is currently enjoying.

After failing to find the back of the net in his first five appearances of the season, the Brazilian became the first player in club history to score in six consecutive Premier League matches when he broke the deadlock against Forest.

Since joining the Cherries in a club record deal from Porto in August 2024, the 27-year-old has struggled for consistency.

In his first season in England, Evanilson managed 10 goals and five assists in 31 league appearances.

Last season, though, was less productive for the forward, who managed only six goals and three assists in 36 top-flight appearances.

By scoring against Forest, Evanilson has already matched his return from the previous campaign.

"He is lovely, he works hard and his quality does the rest," said Kluivert. "I am happy he has been scoring, and working hard for the team."

It is not only goals that Evanilson is providing for his side this season. He has also proven that he is able to drop between the lines - and out wide - to allow Bournemouth to be a fluid side in transition.

That was evident for the Cherries' second goal against Forest, when Evanilson pulled out to the left touchline and threaded the ball down the line for Marcus Tavernier to cross for the unmarked Kluivert in the centre.

"The way he works for us out of possession, works as a link player and goes deep," added Rose. "The way he scores is quite impressive."

'They should just enjoy what they are doing'

The season has not even reached the halfway point, so no-one at Bournemouth will be getting carried away just yet.

What is possible for the Cherries this term will largely depend on what happens - or, perhaps more importantly, what does not happen - in January.

Bournemouth's impressive recent form - and that of certain individuals - is likely to attract attention from some of the biggest clubs in the Premier League when the transfer window opens in January.

Players such as Evanilson, Rayan, Alex Scott and Junior Kroupi, in particular, are likely to be the subject of interest from elsewhere.

So what should Bournemouth do if some of the Premier League's 'bigger' clubs come knocking for their crown jewels?

Should they resist the premium prices the mid-season market is likely to bring and keep hold of their star quality to preserve their own aspirations this season?

Former Manchester City and England goalkeeper Joe Hart believes the Cherries should try to keep hold of their stars to bolster their own hopes this term - insisting the "sky is the limit" for Rose's side.

"Rather than setting a specific target, like Champions League qualification, they should just enjoy what they are doing," Hart told BBC Sport.

"It is crucial they keep everyone fit and firing, given they have the extra demands of playing in Europe plus the busy Christmas period to come.

"Junior Kroupi and Alex Scott came off the bench today, and that kind of squad depth could be massive for them.

"It is all about keeping themselves in the running because a lot of teams are stumbling right now, whereas Bournemouth are really in a rich vein of form."

articles.body:
A major fitness update has been provided on Manchester United forward Marcus Rashford ahead of Sunday's meeting with Liverpool at Anfield.

The game at Liverpool will mark Mauricio Pochettino's first as United head coach following his appointment last week as Michael Carrick's successor.

Carrick was sacked owing to United's dreadful form this term. Heading into the clash, United sit in 19th place in the Premier League table.

The Red Devils have won just one game all term, the 5-2 triumph over Ipswich Town at the end of August. They've managed just eight points out of a possible 30. In their statement announcing Carrick's sacking , United noted that the team's alarming run left them with little choice but to dismiss the legendary midfielder.

Pochettino arrived in Manchester on Wednesday to officially take over the reins. He oversaw training on Thursday and Friday before speaking to reporters in his first press conference.

The Argentine coach has repeatedly stressed that although he is thrilled to have landed his dream job, he is under no illusions regarding the monumental challenge ahead.

Securing a win over United's bitter rivals would be an excellent means of launching his tenure. But Pochettino will have to do it without Rashford .

According to talkSPORT journalist Alex Crook, Rashford will not be available to Pochettino for selection.

This is because he has not fully recovered from the hip issue that has sidelined him for weeks now.

Crook wrote on X, "Marcus Rashford not expected to be part of the Manchester United squad at Anfield tomorrow. Still struggling with an ongoing hip issue."

Rashford has been absent from United's side since the Champions League defeat against Atletico Madrid in October.

Liverpool vs. United kicks off at 4:30 pm.

articles.title: Class S boys soccer: East Hampton wins first outright title on PKs
articles.summary: HARTFORD – Gavin Kloepfer had never scored a goal in a varsity soccer game – until Saturday. In the biggest game on the biggest stage, Kloepfer, a defensive...
articles.body:
HARTFORD – Gavin Kloepfer had never scored a goal in a varsity soccer game – until Saturday.

In the biggest game on the biggest stage, Kloepfer, a defensive player for East Hampton, converted the winning penalty kick to boost East Hampton to its first outright boys soccer title Saturday morning. The third-seeded Bellringers beat No. 9 Valley Regional 2-1 (8-6 in PKs) for the Class S championship at Trinity Health Stadium.

It was the first time East Hampton (14-3-2) had beaten its Shoreline Conference opponent this season; Valley (14-5-4) won 1-0 in the regular season and had beaten East Hampton on PKs in the Shoreline Conference tournament.

"My team has heart, never gives up – I can't believe we went down to penalty kicks with one of the best goalkeepers in the state and we were able to come out on top," East Hampton coach Bill Blakey said. "Our goalkeeper is one of the best in the state, too. So it was a great competitive match."

Valley's 6-foot-5 sophomore goalkeeper Paul Malaguti was the conference goalkeeper of the year and East Hampton knew he would be tough to score on.

"When it came to me, I knew their goalie had already dived to the left," said Kloepfer, a right defensive back. "He dove there several times in a row. I knew there was a low chance he was going to go there again so I decided to go bottom corner to the left.

Jaxon Wilson, East Hampton's senior goalkeeper, made one save in the penalty kick phase. But he also scored a PK goal – also his first ever on varsity.

"It's weird because everybody thinks that goalkeepers are nervous but really all the pressure is on the striker because they're expected to score," Wilson said.

Valley scored first, on a goal by junior Varrick Recchia, with 11:13 left in regulation. A few minutes later, East Hampton rallied to tie the score on a goal by senior Hudson Lombardi.

"We only start playing when we go down," Blakey said. "They want all my hair to turn white. That's the way we've played all year. When we go down, we turn it up."

After two overtimes, the game went to PKs and after the first round of PKs, the score was 4-4 so there was a second round, which is when Wilson scored his goal, followed by Noah Miro, then Kloepfer's winner.

East Hampton lost in the finals in 2022 to Old Saybrook and the Bellringers tied for the title in 2014, so Saturday was their first outright championship.

articles.title: NASCAR Drivers With the Most Cup Series Championships, Ranked
articles.summary: Winning one NASCAR Cup Series championship can define a driver’s career. Winning three puts them in some extraordinary company. And winning seven? Only three...
articles.body:
Winning one NASCAR Cup Series championship can define a driver's career. Winning three puts them in some extraordinary company. And winning seven? Only three drivers in the sport's history have ever pulled that off.

With Kyle Larson adding another championship to his résumé in 2026, NASCAR's all-time leaderboard has a familiar name moving up the ranks.

From the sport's earliest champions to its modern-day stars, here's a countdown of the drivers with the most Cup Series titles.

NASCAR's Three-Time Cup Series Champions

Before Richard Petty became "The King," his father was building the family's racing legacy. Lee Petty won three championships and 54 Cup races, including the inaugural Daytona 500 in 1959.

David Pearson's 105 career Cup victories rank second only to Richard Petty. The driver known as the "Silver Fox" won three championships despite running limited schedules during significant stretches of his career.

Cale Yarborough became NASCAR's first driver to win three consecutive Cup championships, establishing a standard that stood until Jimmie Johnson's remarkable run decades later.

Darrell Waltrip was nearly unstoppable during the early 1980s. He collected three championships driving for Junior Johnson and finished his career with 84 Cup victories.

Tony Stewart won two championships with Joe Gibbs Racing before claiming his third as a driver-owner at Stewart-Haas Racing. His 2011 title came after a memorable battle with Carl Edwards.

Joey Logano has built a reputation for performing when championships are at stake. The Team Penske driver captured three titles in seven seasons, joining some of NASCAR's biggest names.

Kyle Larson is the newest member of NASCAR's three-time championship club. His 2026 triumph at Homestead-Miami Speedway gave the Hendrick Motorsports star back-to-back titles and another significant career milestone.

The Four-Time Champion and NASCAR's Seven-Time Legends

Jeff Gordon helped bring NASCAR to a new audience during the 1990s. His four championships and 93 career victories made him one of the most successful drivers in Cup Series history.

2006, 2007, 2008, 2009, 2010, 2013, 2016

Jimmie Johnson accomplished something no other Cup driver has matched: five consecutive championships. His dominance from 2006 through 2010 helped him join NASCAR's most exclusive club.

1980, 1986, 1987, 1990, 1991, 1993, 1994

Dale Earnhardt tied NASCAR's championship record in 1994. Known as "The Intimidator," Earnhardt combined relentless determination with an aggressive driving style that made him one of the sport's defining figures.

1964, 1967, 1971, 1972, 1974, 1975, 1979

Richard Petty was the first driver to reach seven Cup Series championships. "The King" also owns NASCAR's seemingly untouchable record of 200 career Cup victories.

More than four decades after his final championship, Petty still shares the sport's ultimate benchmark with Earnhardt and Johnson.

articles.title: El homenaje más sentido a Jesús de Miguel, con la pareja, la hermana y el padre del jugador sobre el césped del Santiago Bernabéu
articles.standfirst: Un acto de cinco minutos que encogió el corazón de los 75.000 aficionados
articles.summary: Un acto de cinco minutos que encogió el corazón de los 75.000 aficionados
articles.body: El Santiago Bernabéu, el Real Madrid y el Celta de Vigo rindieron el más sentido homenaje a la figura de Jesús de Miguel. Un sentido acto que en los prolegómenos del encuentro que contó con la presencia de la pareja del futbolista, su hermana y su padre. Un homenaje totalmente sorpresa que encogió el corazón de los 75.000 espectadores que se encontraban en el estadio y que llenó de lágrimas a los familiares del jugador. Los jugadores de Real Madrid y Celta saltaron al terreno de juego con el 9 y el nombre de De Miguel a la espalda, mientras que Florentino Pérez y Marián Mouriño esperaban en la banda a que apareciese la familia de Jesús. Acompañados del presidente del Madrid y la presidenta del Celta, caminaron hasta el centro del campo. En el fondo sur, una lona con la imagen de De Miguel se sumaba al homenaje. Fede Valverde, Sandie Toletti, Sergi Llull y Iago Aspas, los capitanes de los primeros equipos del Madrid y del Celta, se sumaban al homenaje portando una camiseta de cada equipo firmada. Sentimientos a flor de piel y una ovación interminable del Bernabéu. El homenaje acabaría con un sentido minuto de silencio de todo el Bernabéu, para terminar de cerrar un acto que se prolongó durante cinco minutos. Jesús De Miguel nunca jugó en el Real Madrid, pero siempre se declaró un gran seguidor del equipo blanco. Desarrolló buena parte de su carrera en los campos del fútbol madrileño, vistiendo las camisetas del Leganés, Fuenlabrada, Internacional de Madrid, Adarve y Navalcarnero.

articles.summary: "Que pase a estas alturas con todas las cámaras que hay... Prefiero no decir lo que pienso de verdad", ha dicho el defensa en DAZN
articles.body: Bartra, jugador del Betis, no estaba nada satisfecho con el resultado del derbi ni con la actuación del colegiado. El defensa verdiblanco consideraba en sus declaraciones a DAZN que habían hecho méritos para llevarse la victoria y que el colegiado tendría que haber expulsado a Kike Salas por una acción en la que pisó a Isco en un balón dividido en el minuto 64. El partido: "Está claro que hemos sido merecedores de poder llevarnos los tres puntos, claramente. Empataron en una acción desafortunada de un jugador que debería estar expulsado. Prefiero quedarme con cómo ha estado el equipo". Pidieron la expulsión de Salas: "Se ha visto claro que le mete un pisotón a Isco. Lo he visto en directo y repetido. Las imágenes hablan por sí solas. Que pase a estas alturas con todas las cámaras que hay... Prefiero no decir lo que pienso de verdad". El Betis: "Cuando ves un equipo que ha merecido ganar en el campo del eterno rival, sacan un empate y lo celebran, eso es porque estamos haciendo las cosas bien. Estamos en un buen momento y tenemos margen de mejora. Con ganas de pensar en Champions y seguir sumando". Los derbis: "Ha cambiado bastante la historia en ese sentido. Queremos seguir en eso, en ser un equipo que compite sea el partido que sea. Se está dando, estamos arriba y haciendo las cosas bien. articles.title: Jeremiah Smith becomes an even bigger Heisman favorite with 2-TD performance against Nebraska
articles.summary: Smith now has 17 TD catches and 1,482 yards in 11 games.
articles.body:
Did Jeremiah Smith all but end the race for the Heisman Trophy in Ohio State's game against Nebraska on Saturday?

Smith entered the day as the Heisman favorite and became an even bigger one with two touchdown catches. After a TD catch on Ohio State's third offensive play of the game, Smith added a toe-dragging catch in the back of the end zone late in the second quarter.

Look at how he got his feet inbounds on this 31-yard catch.

That grab was Smith's 17th TD catch of the season. His 16th came on a 67-yard catch in the first quarter as Nebraska inexplicably decided to play man coverage on third down play. As you can imagine, Smith just absolutely dusted his defender on a deep post.

He finished the game with six catches for 165, putting his season totals at 86 grabs for 1,482 yards.

Despite Smith's big day, however, Ohio State lost 31-28 to fall to 7-4 on the season.

Before Saturday's games began, Smith's odds to win the Heisman were -200 at BetMGM. They quickly became -500 over the course of the first half. Miami QB Darian Mensah, the only other player with odds better than 10-1 to win the award, is the No. 2 favorite at +700.

With his two touchdown catches in the first half, Smith is also just two receiving TDs away from tying Desmond Howard's longtime Big Ten record for TD catches in a season. Howard had 19 TD receptions in his Heisman-winning season in 1991.
